preamble.summary: Psalm 28 (MT) / Psalm 27 (LXX) is a Davidic cry for rescue from enemies, moving from petition to confidence after divine hearing. 'The LORD is the strength of his people and the saving refuge of his anointed' (v. 8) and the closing 'save your people, shepherd them, carry them forever' (v. 9) provide both royal-kingship and shepherd-theology.
preamble.notable_variants: 28:1 'pit' / 'those who go down to the pit' as Sheol-vocabulary; 28:8 'his anointed' (christou autou) Messianic-royal category; 28:9 'shepherd them and carry them' pastoral-theology.

variant_notes: 'To you I cry, O LORD, my rock!' tracks MT. 'Go down to the pit' (tois katabainousin eis lakkon) — the descent-to-Sheol euphemism for death. Acts 2:27 ('you will not abandon my soul to Hades') inverts the fear with resurrection-confidence.
'Lift my hands toward the inner sanctuary' tracks MT. Hand-lifting-toward-sanctuary is the standard Hebrew-Bible prayer-posture. 1 Tim 2:8 ('lifting holy hands') carries it into NT prayer-tradition.
'Speak peace … while malice in hearts' tracks MT. The double-hearted speech-deception (cf. Ps 12:2) is the anti-integrity target.

'Give them according to their deeds' tracks MT. The retribution-principle that Romans 2:6 ('he will render to each one according to his works') cites: retribution-by-deeds is biblical-ethics constant.
'They do not understand the works of the LORD' tracks MT. The anti-understanding of God's works is the wicked's spiritual-blindness — a theme Isaiah 6 and Romans 11:8–10 develop.
'The LORD is my strength and my shield' tracks MT. Hebrews 13:6 (citing LXX Ps 118:6 'the Lord is my helper') carries similar confidence.

verses.mt_reading: יְהוָה עֹז־לָמוֹ וּמָעוֹז יְשׁוּעוֹת מְשִׁיחוֹ הוּא
verses.lxx_reading: κύριος κραταίωμα τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ ὑπερασπιστὴς τῶν σωτηρίων τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν
verses.mt_rendering: The LORD is the strength of his people and the saving refuge of his anointed
verses.variant_rendering: The Lord is the strength of his people and the shield of the salvations of his anointed
variant_notes: 'HIS ANOINTED' (christou autou) — reprises the Ps 2:2, 18:51, 20:7 christos-royal formula. The king is the Lord's anointed; the Lord is his saving strength. The NT Christological application: Christ himself is the anointed-par-excellence whom the Father saves (Heb 5:7 'was heard because of his reverence').

verses.mt_reading: הוֹשִׁיעָה אֶת־עַמֶּךָ וּבָרֵךְ אֶת־נַחֲלָתֶךָ וּרְעֵם וְנַשְּׂאֵם עַד־הָעוֹלָם
verses.lxx_reading: σῶσον τὸν λαόν σου καὶ εὐλόγησον τὴν κληρονομίαν σου καὶ ποίμανον αὐτοὺς καὶ ἔπαρον αὐτοὺς ἕως τοῦ αἰῶνος
verses.mt_rendering: Save your people and bless your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them forever
verses.variant_rendering: Save your people and bless your inheritance, and shepherd them and lift them up forever
variant_notes: 'SAVE YOUR PEOPLE / BLESS YOUR INHERITANCE.' The 'people and inheritance' pair is the covenantal-formula for Israel. Titus 2:14 ('he gave himself for us … to purify for himself a people of his own possession,' laon periousion) Christologically extends the theme.

'Shepherd them and lift them up forever' — the shepherd-bearing theology that Isaiah 40:11 ('he will gather the lambs in his arms and carry them in his bosom') and John 10:11–16 (Jesus the good shepherd) develop.
